title: Homography warp: a live DOM screen set into a drawing by four corners
intent: A live screen inside a picture
summary: A real HTML app (text, a button, a stepped CSS loop) in a fixed box sized from its scene (at most 640 px, 86 % of the width, 62 % of the height, 16:10) is carried from its flat layout box onto the four corners of a laptop screen drawn in true perspective (projected from a 3D model turned 42°, far edge 0.68 of the near one): the corners are read off an SVG polygon through `getScreenCTM()`, so the drawing's crop and scale are included (cover on wide frames, the lid fitted across 92 % of a phone's width), and re-read by a ResizeObserver; the scroll through a `280svh` sticky stage, smoothstepped over `.12–.78` of it, lerps each corner from flat to target, and the 2D homography from the rectangle to those points (eight unknowns, Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting) is written as one `matrix3d` with `transform-origin: 0 0`, `none` at the start; the browser hit-tests, selects and focuses through the same matrix; a shadow and a glare inside the screen trade opacity with the landing (`1 − e`, `e`) so the scrub only composites; one scroll listener and one frame; the loop runs only while playing, on screen and on a visible tab, behind the app's own button and a 44 px page-level control with a polite status; reduced motion and static get no rail and sit placed and paused
variants: scrubbed from flat into the drawing (this, default)
always placed: the same solve on load and on resize only, for device mock-ups in a case study
a <video> or canvas in place of the app, warped into a photograph whose corners are given as fractions of the image
